title: Leaving New York for Dallas: a club, a wife and returning in 1954
summary: A legal problem sends him to Montreal and Dallas, where he plays at Kane's Hitching Post, marries Nancy, and returns to New York.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: You certainly did a lot of. Did you go back to Texas for..

Yes. I went back to Texas, I'll tell you why. There was some problem here and it would have been a question of some litigation, so a lawyer decided that perhaps I should not, you know, should not be around in New York for a while. So I

went to Montreal and from Montreal I went to Dallas. And a friend of mine owned a club there and was in the undertaking business and we were/going to do some business in the undertaking business, and I suggested to him, "Why not put a piano in this club," and I would, you know, play at night for a little while. So this is what he did. He put a piano in his club and I stayed there for a while. And the undertaking business began to thrive.

But I went out...I went out to Kane's Hitching Post... that was a restaurant in Dallas. And I went out to Kane's Hitching Post and got a job with a drummer named Spoons. And then I played there and stayed around Dallas for two or three years, opened a couple of night clubs, lost a lot of money...

Well, one of the things I gained in Dallas in '52 was I gained a wife. I married Nancy and shortly after...in '54... I decided that I'd had it with Dallas. Because you're in a rut, you see. You know, you long for New York and other places. You see, all of your friends come through on the road shows and tell you, "Man, what are you wasting your time..." So finally I came back to New York.
